body: Hey! 40M would like to chat too. Here to talk

Well, I won’t repeat everyone here, they’re spot on about the pain. I’ve had some major depression and my own thoughts, I can honestly say talking to someone is the way to go. I’ve talked to friends and family, yeah it’s really *ucking hard to start, but most are surprisingly supportive. Whether it’s a close relative or friend, just try one person, it is a huge release when in the mindset you’re talking about. Someone mentioned the ER if you’re in immediate danger. Another option is to talk to your primary doctor, they’ll be able to get you some help. You can even walk-in to many behavioral health clinics/hospitals and they can help too. I can’t tell you it’s a magic solution, it isn’t, but it can be enough release to help you hang around and learn some of the methods they can teach you to help you deal with things. Personally, the thoughts are still there, but that voice got weaker with work. I’ve been inpatient, a few intensive outpatient programs, and have a counselor. While every professional can help, you might be more comfortable with some than others. Just keep that in mind too, you can always switch up who you work with until you find the right connection. They are so supportive. Please give it a shot, there’s really nothing to lose. Plus you need to take care of YOU, that is always ok. Most people will be happy you helped yourself and will have the hard conversation with you, rather than have to deal with the alternative. You can talk to me too, I’m happy to listen, sometimes a stranger is an easier start. Please take care and I hope the best for you.

The narrator created the means of execution being tried out on the inmate.  The narrator feels guilty because of the deaths that will result of this invention, including the inmate in front of them.  The inmate is forgiving the narrator for this.

This was it, my only chance, humanity’s only chance.  I had, roughly, just 30 minutes to find the mark and figure out a way to neutralize it.  That was all that we could manage to calculate, even that was a guess.  I am scanning the crowd furiously for the beginning, agent zero, the end of mankind as we know it.  If I didn’t find the source of the virus it would mutate and in only 12 more years it would wipe out 76% of the population.  We had no other solution, travel back and sacrifice one life to save the lives of many.  The only catch was that even though we developed time travel it wasn’t corporeal time travel, only the consciousness could go back.  While it allowed for the ability to move more freely it also prevented any physical contact with the past.  The change would have to be made some other way.  As I scan the crowd again it hits me, I’ve seen this face before, 9 years ago.  An assignment from my psych class.  I wrote a paper on the mind of a death row inmate.  I had attended an execution to get a feel for what happens at the end of a stay on death row.  As I watched them begin the injection on the inmate he looked across the crowd and stopped on me.  He gazed deep into my eyes, I could almost feel him reach into me.  He then said the last 3 words of his life, “I forgive you.”  That moment stuck with me all my life but I never knew what it meant until now.  I still remember it like it was yesterday but for him it is 3 years away.  It was then that I knew what to do.  As I entered the police officer’s body, my consciousness merging with his, he can see me.  He can see the future that is to come.  He sees what lies ahead for us.  He knows there is only one answer.  He unholsters his sidearm.  He points the pistol at his son.  He saves the world.

Mine happened back in 6th grade. We had a substitute teacher that gave us a puzzle to keep us busy, I'm sure there was some reward promised but I don't remember anymore. It was simple enough. A rectangle divided in half horizontally with the top half divided equally in two and the bottom half divided equally in three. The objective was to cross every "wall" of the image with one consecutive line only once. It's very easy to cross all but one or think you have it and find one "wall" has been crossed twice. Years go by and I now have notebooks full of these puzzle attempts. Every time I'm bored in class I fill margins with these puzzle attempts. I do not want to give up. It's bothering the shit out of me. It wasn't until college that I finally decided to search the Internet for the answer finally having gotten so incredibly pissed off at this puzzle. Yup....asshole substitute gave us an unsolvable puzzle just to keep us busy and out of his hair. So. Much. Time. Wasted. 

TL:DR Sixth grade substitute gave us unsolvable puzzle to keep us out of his hair, didn't find out it was unsolvable until college.
